name: Prepare TIER and federal emissions reports
summary: Each spring the emissions team turns a year of continuous emissions monitoring, fuel and generation data into the facility reports that set the company's carbon bill and meet federal reporting rules. For each large thermal facility it calculates the Alberta TIER obligation against the 0.370 t/MWh electricity benchmark, has the report verified by a third party, settles the obligation with credits or fund payments chosen by the marketing desk and files by June 30; for every reporting facility it files federal greenhouse gas, pollutant inventory and gas-generation regulation reports by June 1. The work is slow because all reports fall due in the same few months, because the CEMS and fuel records must be reconciled, and because verification and sign-off queues sit between a small team and fixed deadlines.

baseline.org_archetype: An Alberta generator with about four TIER-regulated thermal facilities, about seven federally reporting facilities and a four-person emissions team, paying 160 to 205 million CAD a year in carbon compliance company-wide.
baseline.notes: Carbon compliance cost and benchmark from the modelled company's filings; facility counts, report mix and step times are estimates.

unit_of_work: one compliance report (one facility, one program, one year)
trigger: The reporting year closes and validated CEMS data for the facility is available.
end_state: The report is filed with AEP or ECCC, any TIER obligation is settled by credits or fund payment, and regulator questions are closed.

volume.seasonality: Nearly all work falls between January and June: federal reports are due June 1 and TIER reports June 30, so the team's load in those months is about twice the yearly average and close to nothing from July to December except regulator questions.

evidence.note: About 20 to 24 reports a year (4 TIER, 6 GHGRP, 7 NPRI, 3-5 federal coal or gas-generation regulation reports) from the facility list in the organisation file; TIER threshold 100,000 t (src1) and GHGRP threshold 10,000 t (src3) set which facilities report.

Does the quantification, verification support and filings required in src1 and src3; four analysts also handle credits, forecasts and other approvals. Loaded cost from the organisation file (wage x 1.40: benefits about 25 percent, overhead about 15 percent).
Estimates NPRI pollutant releases and peer-reviews federal reports; share estimated. Loaded cost from the organisation file (wage x 1.40: benefits about 25 percent, overhead about 15 percent).

systems.name: Energy trading and risk management system
AER and Alberta Environment submission portals
Document management and engineering drawings repository
ECCC Single Window reporting system (GHGRP and NPRI)
Alberta emissions offset and EPC registry

steps.name: Extract annual CEMS, fuel and generation data
steps.description: After year-end and the last quarterly CEMS audits, the emissions analyst pulls hourly CO2, NOx and SO2 data from the CEMS data system, fuel gas flows and gross and net generation from the plant historian into the facility quantification workbook. Reports are worked in deadline order, so federal ones wait behind TIER packages.

error.defect_description: Wrong date range or unit tag pulled.

evidence.note: Start lag reflects year-end close and the order in which a small team works its reports; author estimate.

steps.name: Check CEMS data quality and substituted hours
steps.description: The analyst checks each hour flagged as missing or out of control, confirms the substitution method used, compares results with the year's relative accuracy test and calibration records, and notes any hours that need correction.

control.basis: Alberta CEMS Code and SOR/2018-261 s. 16 CEMS quality assurance

evidence.note: CEMS certification and audit duty in src5 s. 16; Alberta CEMS Code named from general knowledge.

steps.name: Supply fuel volumes and net generation
steps.description: A settlement analyst in marketing sends the year's metered fuel gas volumes from pipeline statements and net-to-grid energy from AESO settlement, which the emissions team uses as an independent check.

error.defect_description: Volumes for the wrong facility boundary.

evidence.note: Common cross-check between CEMS and fuel records; author estimate.

steps.name: Reconcile CEMS CO2 against fuel-based CO2
steps.description: The analyst calculates CO2 from fuel volumes and gas composition and compares it with the CEMS total. A gap above the analyst's tolerance goes to the plant; otherwise the work moves to the report it is for.

error.defect_description: Gas composition or emission factor out of date.

evidence.note: Report mix from facility counts: about 4 TIER reports, 6 GHGRP, 7 NPRI and 3-5 federal coal or gas regulation reports a year; shares estimated.

steps.name: Investigate the discrepancy with the plant
steps.description: The plant engineer checks meter calibrations, CEMS probe faults and unit events in the historian to explain the gap and tells the analyst which source to correct.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Calculate the TIER obligation
steps.description: For a TIER facility the analyst multiplies net generation by the 0.370 t/MWh benchmark, subtracts it from total emissions and prices the shortfall at the year's fund price, writing up the compliance report form with all quantification methods.

error.defect_description: Benchmark applied to gross instead of net output.

control.basis: TIER Regulation: facility benchmark and compliance obligation

evidence.note: Benchmark 0.370 t CO2e/MWh in src2; obligation options in src1.

steps.name: Assemble the verification package and brief the verifier
steps.description: The analyst gathers the workbook, CEMS audit reports, meter calibration records and procedures into a shared folder, holds a kickoff call with the third-party verifier and books the site visit.

evidence.note: Third-party assurance required (src1); wait is the verifier's booking slot in the spring rush.

steps.name: Verifier tests the data and visits the site
steps.description: The external verifier samples hours and meters, re-performs calculations, interviews plant staff and visits the facility, then sends a list of queries and findings.

control.basis: TIER Regulation: third-party assurance of compliance reports

evidence.note: Requirement in src1; duration estimated.

steps.name: Answer verifier queries and correct errors
steps.description: The analyst answers each query, pulls the records the verifier asks for, corrects misstatements in the workbook and the draft report, and re-sends the revised figures with evidence.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Verifier issues its statement
steps.description: The verifier completes its review and issues the verification report and statement. If a material misstatement remains, it goes back to the analyst for another round.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Send the obligation to marketing
steps.description: The analyst sends the verified tonnes owed for the facility to the environmental credits desk in marketing so it can choose which credits to use.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Choose credits and fund payment mix
steps.description: The term trader compares the cost of offsets and emission performance credits in inventory (many from the company's own hydro and wind) with the fund price, reserves the credits to retire and confirms the fund payment amount.

error.defect_description: Credit vintage or type not eligible for the year.

evidence.note: Compliance options in src1; own offsets and EPCs from renewables in src2; time estimated.

steps.name: Director reviews and signs the compliance report
steps.description: The director of health, safety, environment and regulatory reviews the verified report, the obligation and its cost, and signs it for submission, or sends it back with questions.

control.basis: TIER compliance report signed by the person responsible for the facility

evidence.note: Signing requirement from general knowledge; time estimated.

steps.name: Submit the report, retire credits and pay the fund
steps.description: Before June 30 the analyst uploads the report and verification statement to the Alberta submission system, retires the chosen credits in the registry and requests the fund payment from treasury.

error.defect_description: Credit serial numbers mistyped in the registry.

control.basis: TIER Regulation: verified compliance report due June 30

evidence.note: June 30 deadline in src1.

steps.name: Wait for AEP acknowledgement
steps.description: Alberta Environment and Parks logs the report and the credit retirement. In some years it follows up with questions on methods or credits.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Answer AEP questions on the report
steps.description: Weeks or months after filing, the analyst answers AEP's questions on methods or credits, sends supporting records from the verification file and, if needed, files a corrected report.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Estimate NPRI pollutant releases
steps.description: For the pollutant inventory the environmental specialist estimates NOx, SO2, particulate, mercury and other listed substances from CEMS, stack tests and emission factors, and checks each against the reporting thresholds.

error.defect_description: Emission factor out of date or threshold misread.

evidence.note: NPRI quantification practice; author estimate.

steps.name: Enter the report in ECCC Single Window
steps.description: The analyst keys the facility's emissions, production and methods into the federal Single Window system, which feeds the federal greenhouse gas program, the pollutant inventory and the Alberta greenhouse gas reporting that shares the system, and attaches required auditor reports.

error.defect_description: Keying error or wrong unit of measure.

evidence.note: Single Window named in src4; GHGRP duty in src3; time estimated.

steps.name: Peer review the report
steps.description: The environmental specialist compares the draft with last year's report and the workbook, checks large year-on-year changes have an explanation, and returns it if anything is wrong.

control.basis: Department four-eyes review of regulatory submissions

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Director certifies and submits
steps.description: The director, as the certifying official, reviews the summary and submits the report in Single Window before June 1, making the legal certification of accuracy.

control.basis: GHGRP and NPRI notices under CEPA and SOR/2018-261 s. 21: report and certify by June 1

evidence.note: June 1 deadline in src3 and src5.

steps.name: ECCC validates the submission
steps.description: ECCC's system and staff check the report for completeness and unusual values. Most reports are accepted; some come back with data-quality questions.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Answer ECCC data-quality questions
steps.description: Over the summer the analyst looks up each value ECCC flagged, explains it from the workbook or corrects it, and resubmits the report in Single Window.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

exceptions.name: CEMS and fuel records disagree
exceptions.description: The CEMS total and the fuel-based CO2 differ by more than tolerance and the plant must find the cause before the report can proceed.

exceptions.name: Material misstatement at verification
exceptions.description: About one in ten TIER reports needs a second round of corrections before the verifier signs.

exceptions.name: Regulator questions after filing
exceptions.description: AEP or ECCC asks about methods, credits or unusual values weeks after filing and the analyst must answer or refile.

exceptions.name: Federal report returned at peer review
exceptions.description: The peer reviewer finds a keying error or unexplained change and sends the draft back.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from year-end to filing
benchmarks.population: Facility emissions reports filed to statutory deadlines

evidence.note: Deadlines of June 1 (day 152, src3, src5) and June 30 (day 181, src1) cap the cycle; filers usually submit in the last weeks before the deadline (tier C).

pain_points.description: Every report falls due within a four-week window, so a four-person team works reports in deadline order and federal reports wait behind TIER verification.

evidence.note: June 1 and June 30 deadlines.

pain_points.description: Verifiers are booked by many facilities in the same spring weeks, so the site visit date sets the timeline.

evidence.note: Author estimate from the shared June 30 deadline.

pain_points.description: CEMS data, fuel meter records and settlement volumes sit in different systems and must be pulled and reconciled by hand in spreadsheets.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

pain_points.description: Errors carry a direct cost: at 30 to 50 CAD a tonne, a 1 percent error on a 3 Mt facility is 0.9 to 1.5 million CAD.

evidence.note: Fund price of 50 CAD in 2022 (src2), compliance cost in src6; facility size estimated.

sources.title: Technology Innovation and Emissions Reduction Regulation
sources.supports: TIER applies to facilities emitting 100,000 t CO2e or more a year in 2016 or later; verified annual compliance reports are due by June 30 of the following year; compliance and benchmark reports need third-party assurance; obligations met by on-site reductions, emission offsets, emission performance credits or TIER fund credits.

assumptions: One case is one report for one facility and one program. Report types share the data and reconciliation steps (s01-s05), then split: TIER (s06-s16), and federal GHGRP, NPRI and coal or gas-generation regulation reports (s17-s22). The split probabilities at s04 are applied after any reconciliation loop.
The organisation file's mode of 1 report a month is low: the facility list implies about 20 to 24 reports a year (1.8 a month), all prepared in January to June.

The organisation file has no external party for the third-party GHG verifier, so verifier steps use the role 'external'. ECCC Single Window and the Alberta credit registry are added as systems because the organisation file lacks them.
Emission credits arrive mid-case from marketing (s12), so they are listed as an input rather than a trigger.

TIER replaced the Carbon Competitiveness Incentive Regulation on 1 January 2020; the 2019 compliance year was reported in 2020 under similar verification and June 30 rules. This continuity rests on general knowledge.

Converted units first fall under SOR/2018-261 annual reporting only once its limits apply; in 2019-2022 the federal coal-fired regulations applied to the coal units, and their reports are treated the same as other federal reports here.
The simulated 90th percentile (about 220 days) exceeds the 178-day benchmark because the simulation includes regulator questions answered after filing (s16, s22) while the benchmark stops at filing.

Alberta CEMS Code and the TIER signing requirement are named from general knowledge; those documents were not opened. The TIER verification standard could not be opened (server error), so verification steps are tier B or C.
